page: Amazon Web Services d3.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, providing 32 virtual CPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. System memory includes 256 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. The defining hardware attribute is its integrated high-density local storage subsystem, providing 47,520 GB of raw capacity on hard disk drives. Network connectivity offers a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reflect the characteristics of its second-generation Intel scalable architecture. Multi-threaded processing capabilities fall within the middle tier across tests, scoring 27,102.24 in stress-ng multi-core CPU and 9,833.0 in Geekbench multi-core. In contrast, single-thread performance is comparatively low, registering 1,088.0 in Geekbench single-core, 1,286.19 in stress-ng single-core, and weak throughput in gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Large-block uncached memory operations register 112.35 GB/s for reads and 48.12 GB/s for writes, while PassMark database operations achieved 10,877.51 points and Redis SET throughput reached 26.36 million operations per second.

The primary efficiency tradeoff of the d3.8xlarge lies in its dense mechanical local storage coupled with moderate multi-core compute capability. While magnetic storage limits random IOPS relative to solid-state alternatives, it enables massive sequential data storage per instance. This makes the d3.8xlarge functionally suited for sequential big data processing, distributed file systems such as HDFS, MapReduce clusters, log aggregation pipelines, and bulk data analytics where storage capacity per node is prioritized over single-threaded compute speed.
description: Amazon Web Services d3.8xlarge is a dense storage-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, presenting 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 256 GB of DDR4 memory. High-capacity local persistence is delivered via 47,520 GB of bundled HDD storage, supported by 25 Gbps of baseline networking. Benchmark evaluations establish that multi-threaded computational workloads, memory transfers, and Redis key-value operations align with mid-range baselines, whereas single-core processing metrics rank in lower percentiles. The combination of extensive magnetic storage capacity and moderate compute density defines this hardware configuration for massive scale sequential workloads, distributed data lakes, log aggregation architectures, and large Hadoop or analytics clusters.
